steps.title: Prepare coating solution
steps.instruction: Mix 95 mL 95 % ethanol with 5 mL ddH₂O, add 1.2 g poly(methacrylacid‑2‑hydroxyethylester) (120 mg/mL final) to a total volume of 100 mL. The solution is not sterilized after mixing; ethanol provides sterility. After applying to plates, sterilize by UV or filter through 0.25 µm if desired.

steps.title: Coat low‑attachment plates
steps.instruction: Add 150 µL of the coating solution to each well of a 24‑well low‑attachment plate, let the ethanol evaporate overnight, then store the plates at room temperature until use.

steps.title: Prepare Matrigel coating for PSC dishes
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.5 mL Matrigel in 24.5 mL DMEM/F12, add 2 mL of this solution to each 35‑mm dish, polymerize at 37 °C for 2 h (or overnight at room temperature), then UV‑sterilize before use.

steps.title: Maintain human pluripotent stem cells
steps.instruction: Day ‑3: Split hiPSC colonies at a 1:3–1:4 ratio when they reach ~70 % confluency. Discard media, rinse with PBS, incubate with TrypLE for 3–5 min at 37 °C, stop with basal DMEM/F12, spin at 400 rpm for 5 min, discard supernatant, and plate cells in TeSR‑E8 (or StemFlex) medium supplemented with 10 µM Y‑27632 onto freshly Matrigel‑coated 35‑mm dishes (2 mL per dish). Change TeSR‑E8 daily for two days, using 2 mL per dish.

steps.title: Prepare PVA solution for hanging drops
steps.instruction: Dissolve 40 mg polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) in 10 mL TeSR‑E8/StemFlex medium, filter through a 0.25 µm filter, and supplement with 10 µM Y‑27632 and 1 % penicillin/streptomycin (P/S).

steps.title: Generate embryoid bodies (hanging drop)
steps.instruction: Day ‑1: Detach hiPSCs as in step 3, spin, and resuspend in TeSR‑E8/StemFlex containing 10 µM Y‑27632, 1 % P/S and the prepared PVA solution. Count cells and adjust to 200 000 cells/mL (4 000 cells per 20 µL). Place 20 µL drops on the lid of a 10‑cm dish, fill the dish with PBS to maintain humidity, and incubate overnight at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Embed embryoid bodies in Matrigel
steps.instruction: Day 0: Verify EBs are 200–250 µm. Wash EBs into a dish with DMEM/F12. Under a stereoscope, transfer each EB onto Parafilm, remove excess media leaving ~5 µL DMEM/F12, add 30 µL cold Matrigel drop, gently resuspend 2–3× to mix the EB within the droplet, and reposition the EB at the centre of the drop with a 200 µL pipette. Incubate the Matrigel‑embedded EBs at 37 °C for 20–25 min to polymerize.

steps.title: Transfer embedded EBs to low‑attachment wells
steps.instruction: Using a cut‑off 1 000 µL pipette tip, wash the embedded EB droplets into a 10‑cm dish with fresh DMEM/F12, then transfer each droplet into a well of a low‑attachment 24‑well plate containing 1 mL pre‑warmed Differentiation media 1 (Di‑CL). Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Perform partial media changes daily (remove ~75 % of the volume and add fresh medium). Handle plates at ≤45° tilt and aspirate slowly to avoid damaging the Matrigel droplet.

steps.title: Prepare differentiation media
steps.instruction: Prepare the following media (each 100 mL) using sterile technique:

substeps.instruction: Di‑CL: 96 mL DMEM/F12, 1 mL L‑Glutamine (2 mM), 1 mL ITS‑G, 1 mL NEAA, 1 mL P/S (500 U/mL), 100 µL CHIR‑99021 (3 µM), 100 µL LDN‑193189 (0.5 µM).
Di‑CLF (optional): same as Di‑CL plus 50 µL bFGF (10 ng/mL).
Di‑CLFR: same as Di‑CL plus 25 µL bFGF (5 ng/mL) and 10 µL retinoic acid (10 nM).
Di‑LSW: 96 mL DMEM/F12, 1 mL L‑Glutamine, 1 mL ITS‑G, 1 mL NEAA, 1 mL P/S, 100 µL LDN‑193189 (0.5 µM), 100 µL SHH (34 ng/mL), 200 µL WNT1A (20 ng/mL).
Di‑HF: 96 mL DMEM/F12, 1 mL L‑Glutamine, 1 mL ITS‑G, 1 mL NEAA, 1 mL P/S, 100 µL HGF (10 ng/mL), 50 µL bFGF (10 ng/mL).
Di‑X‑H: 96 mL DMEM/F12, 1 mL L‑Glutamine, 1 mL ITS‑X, 1 mL NEAA, 1 mL P/S, 100 µL HGF (10 ng/mL).
Day 3: Replace 75 % of Di‑CL with Di‑CLF.
Day 5: Replace 75 % of Di‑CLF with Di‑CLFR.
Day 7: Replace 75 % of Di‑CLFR with Di‑LSW; thereafter change every second day.
Day 11: Replace 75 % of Di‑LSW with Di‑HF; change every second day.
Day 15: Replace 75 % of Di‑HF with Di‑X‑H; change every second day.
From Day 30 onward: change media every third day.
FACS‑buffer (25 mL): 18.24 mL PBS 1×, 0.1 mL EDTA (2 mM), 6.66 mL BSA (2 %).
Blocking buffer (20 mL): 18.24 mL PBS 1×, 5.33 mL BSA (2 %), 2 mL goat serum (NGS, 10 %).

steps.title: Immunostain organoid sections
steps.instruction: Fix organoids in 4 % paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS overnight at 4 °C with shaking. Dehydrate in 30 % sucrose in PBS overnight, embed in Tissue‑Tek O.C.T., and cryosection at 20–30 µm. Rehydrate sections in PBS, permeabilize with 0.1 % Tween‑20 for 10 min, rinse 3× with PBS, then permeabilize with 0.1 % Triton X‑100 for 10 min and rinse 3×. Block with blocking buffer for 1 h at room temperature (use blocking buffer containing only 2 % BSA for goat primary antibodies). Incubate with primary antibodies overnight at 4 °C, wash 3× 10 min with PBS, incubate with secondary antibodies for 2 h at room temperature, wash, mount with DAPI‑containing mounting medium, and image on a confocal microscope. Sections are stable for months at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare papain dissociation solution
steps.instruction: Mix 30 mL DMEM/F12 with 36 mg papain (0.3 M), 8 mg EDTA (2 %), and 8 mg L‑cysteine (10 %).

steps.title: Generate single‑cell suspension for scRNA‑seq
steps.instruction: Incubate organoids in papain solution for 1 h (or alternatively treat with TrypLE Select for 15 min at 37 °C, then mechanically dissociate by pipetting). Estimate cell number and viability, then resuspend cells in PBS containing 0.5 % BSA to a concentration of 390 cells/µL.

steps.title: Construct scRNA‑seq libraries
steps.instruction: Use the Chromium Single Cell 3′ Library & Gel Bead Kit v3 (Single Cell 3′ Library & Gel Bead Kit v3, Single Cell B Chip Kit, i7 Multiplex Kit) following the manufacturer’s protocol. Sequence libraries on an Illumina HiSeq 3000 (or equivalent) with 150 bp paired‑end reads.

steps.title: Isolate CD82⁺ cells by FACS
steps.instruction: Dissociate SMOs with TrypLE Select for 45 min at 37 °C, performing mechanical pipetting up/down at 25 min and 45 min (3–4 times every 15–20 min). Stop the reaction by adding 3–4 × the volume of FACS‑buffer, filter through a 40 µm cell strainer, and centrifuge. Resuspend the cell pellet in FACS‑buffer, then label 1 × 10⁶ cells with 5 µL PE‑anti‑human CD82 and 5 µL APC‑anti‑human CD56 in 100 µL FACS‑buffer; incubate on ice for 1 h. Centrifuge at 400 rpm for 5 min at room temperature, resuspend in FACS‑buffer with DAPI, and sort CD82⁺ (and CD56⁺ if desired) cells using a FACS sorter. Use unstained SMO cells as controls.

steps.title: Transplant CD82⁺ cells into mouse tibialis anterior
steps.instruction: In 2–3‑month‑old male HsdCpb:NMRI‑Foxn1nu mice, injure the tibialis anterior (TA) muscle by injecting 10 µL cardiotoxin (CTX) at 40 ng/mL 24 h before transplantation. Under anesthesia, inject 1 × 10⁵ CD82⁺ cells in 10 µL PBS into the TA of one hindlimb. Six weeks later, euthanize the mice, harvest the TA, fix in 4 % PFA (in PBS), embed in O.C.T., and cryosection at 10–20 µm thickness.

substeps.instruction: Rehydrate sections in PBS.

Heat sections in citrate buffer (final 19 nM) prepared by mixing 82 mL sodium citrate solution (0.1 M) with 18 mL citric acid solution (0.1 M) and 900 mL ddH₂O; bring to boil and cook at 95 °C for 15 min for antigen retrieval.
Incubate sections with AffiniPure Fab Fragment Goat Anti‑Mouse IgG for 60 min at room temperature.
Permeabilize with 1 % Triton X‑100 and 125 mM glycine in PBS for 20 min at room temperature.
Block with blocking buffer for 60 min at room temperature.
Incubate with primary antibody overnight at 4 °C.
Wash three times 10 min with PBS.
Incubate with secondary antibody for 2 h at room temperature.
Mount and image using Zeiss Scan.Z1 and process with Zen Lite Blue.

description: Validation of protocol The reproducibility of the protocol has been described within various paragraphs of the corresponding article Mavrommatis et al. (2023). The organoid approach was evaluated with six hiPSC lines with independent genetic backgrounds, with more than five independent derivations per line, for the control line (CB CD34+) with more than 20 derivations, always obtaining similar results. The organoids show very reproducible sizes during their development ( Figure 1B of Mavrommatis et al. [18]). To further evaluate the reproducibility of organoid development, diffusion map analysis on qPCR-based expression analysis of 32 genes was applied at early stages, as well as integrative analysis on scRNAseq datasets of mature stages of organoid development from four independent iPSC lines. The data indicate highly conserved cluster representation of myogenic progenitors at all states, together with skeletal muscle myofibers, fibroadipogenic progenitors, and neural progenitors-related clusters (Figure 4, Supplemental Figure 6, Mavrommatis et al. [18]).
